title: Looper
events_chronological: By 2074 time travel exists, is outlawed, and is used only by syndicates to send victims thirty years back to loopers waiting in Kansas cornfields.
In 2044 Joe kills the hooded men sent to him, collects his silver, takes eyedrop narcotics and banks half his pay for Paris.
Joe's handler Abe tells him to learn Chinese and go to Shanghai instead of Paris.
Joe's friend Seth lets his own older self run, and Abe's men carve messages into young Seth until the old one is drawn back and killed.
Joe gives up Seth's hiding place to Abe to get his silver back.
Joe's older self arrives in the cornfield without a hood, knocks him out and escapes, leaving the loop unclosed.
In the thirty years between, Joe survives Shanghai, becomes an enforcer, meets a woman and gives up the drugs for her.
The Rainmaker's men come for Joe, kill his wife in the raid, and send him back to be closed.
Abe's men take Joe's silver and hunt both versions of him across the city.
Old Joe wipes out a squad of gat men in a diner ambush and tells Joe he means to kill the child who will grow up to be the Rainmaker.
Joe takes the map of three candidate children and drives out to the Kansas farm of Sara and her son Cid.
Cid, a telekinetic child, kills a farmhand in a rage, and Sara admits she is his mother and left him for years.
Old Joe hunts down and kills the first two children on his list.
Kid Blue and Abe's men trace Joe to the farm and are torn apart by Cid.
Old Joe reaches the farm to kill Cid and shoots Sara instead.
Joe sees that Cid will become the Rainmaker if he watches his mother die, and shoots himself in the chest, erasing Old Joe.
Sara lives, and holds her son in the road.
syuzhet_notes: The film runs mostly forward through 2044, and its one large displacement is told-order bullets 9-10: a montage of the thirty years Old Joe lived between the two ends of his own loop, dropped into the middle of the runtime to explain why he is running. Before that, the film also plays one version of the cornfield meeting in which Joe closes his loop and lives out those years, then rewinds and plays the version in which he does not.
fabula_notes: Time travel makes a strict chronology ambiguous here - Old Joe's memories change as his younger self acts, and the thirty years in bullets 7-8 are erased outright by bullet 16 - so the ordering follows each character's personal timeline rather than a single world clock. The discarded branch in which Joe closes his loop is folded into bullets 7-8.
